column1: # PURPOSE: bind every load-bearing assertion of this project to the source ids that support it,
# and state what would falsify it. This is the file that makes the memory/knowledge store's
# provenance real rather than decorative: a claim with no source row here must not be asserted.
# FORMAT: tab-separated. One row per claim.
#   id            stable claim id. Cited from prose. Never reuse.
#   claim         the assertion, stated so it COULD be wrong.
#   sources       semicolon-separated SRC ids. Empty is a defect, not a value.
#   falsifier     what observation would disprove it. "—" is a defect for anything but inference.
#   affects       project areas this claim constrains. Comma-separated.
#   established  — directly stated in a primary source, quoted.
#   supported    — multiple sources agree, or one source with measured results.
#   inference    — this project's own reasoning over sourced facts. MUST be labelled as such
#                  wherever it appears in prose. Inferences are allowed to be wrong.
#   contested    — sources disagree, or a vendor claim with no independent verification.
# RULE: an `inference` row must cite the sources it reasons *from*. Reasoning from nothing is not
# an inference, it is an invention — see AGENTS.md non-negotiable 1.

column8: CCS v1.0.0, CC BY 3.0. Format: <type>[optional scope]: <description>.

column2: Only feat and fix carry mandated semantic meaning, and other types are explicitly permitted.
column5: A revision making the wider type set mandatory.
column8: The wider set (build, chore, ci, docs, style, refactor, perf, test) comes via @commitlint/config-conventional, which SRC-072 references. Implication: the type set must be CLOSED BY US and versioned, since the spec permits arbitrary extension.

column2: the prior substrate already follows Conventional Commits in 14 of 15 commits, so the task taxonomy requires no retrofit and no classifier for historical data.
column5: A the prior substrate history showing substantial non-CCS commits.
column8: Read via git log. Only the initial commit is non-CCS. This is why a machine-learning classification problem reduces to a string parse.

column2: Commit classification can be done training-free with few-shot LLM prompting, and chain-of-thought adds no benefit.
column5: A reproduction where chain-of-thought outperforms few-shot for this task.
column8: Balanced 3,200-commit InfluxDB dataset; three models. Model scale matters. Only needed for commits where the label is missing or ambiguous.

column2: A large labelled commit-classification benchmark exists, with AST-level change data and semantic what/why annotations.
column5: Unavailability of the benchmark or its annotations.
column8: 63,533 commits, 243 repositories, 7 languages. Gives free validation data and a supplementary AST axis if commit messages prove insufficient.

column2: Conventional Commits describes commits, not sessions or work items, so the task unit must be chosen separately from the taxonomy.
column5: A specification that also defines session or work-item units.
column8: INFERENCE from the scope of SRC-072. Drives the recommendation to make the WORK ITEM the primary task unit, with commits as the granular layer.

column2: Code-LLM and agent benchmark coverage is heavily skewed toward the software development phase.
column5: A survey showing balanced SDLC coverage.
column8: 181 benchmarks / 461 papers: ~60% development, 5% requirements, 3% design. Our work is development-phase, so the best-instrumented region is where we operate.

column2: Some upgrades are motivated by latency rather than token cost, which conflicts with the multiple-baseline requirement of one consistent metric across cases.
column5: A metric that meaningfully captures both latency-motivated and token-motivated upgrades.
column8: INFERENCE. Concrete instance: the 80 ms mux coalescing was a latency change, whose natural metric is time/task - the noisier instrument per CLM-METRIC-01. Either measure it on time with a noise caveat, or exclude it as a case.

column2: Multiple-baseline tiers must be similar enough that the same intervention and measure make sense, and independent enough that treating one does not change another before its planned start.
column5: A valid multiple-baseline in which tiers share neither intervention nor measure.
column8: THE RULE THAT RESOLVES Q1h. Comparability and independence are dual requirements; neither is optional.

column2: In a multiple-baseline, untreated tiers must remain at baseline while another tier is intervened on; movement in an untreated tier compromises experimental control.
column5: A valid multiple-baseline in which untreated tiers move with the treated tier.
column8: Converted into a TESTABLE requirement in section 28d: does component B tokens/task stay flat when component A is upgraded?

column2: A tier count of three or more with phase changes at three different time points is the WWC three-demonstration convention for multiple-baseline designs.
column5: A revision of the WWC convention, or a valid multiple-baseline below three tiers.
column8: Our design has exactly three admissible token-motivated cases - admissible with ZERO margin.

column2: Meeting a tier count cannot rescue dependent tiers or an invalid measure.
column5: Evidence that tier count alone can establish a functional relation.
column8: The hard line: excluding a non-comparable case is required, not optional, even at the cost of the tier count.

column2: A nonconcurrent multiple baseline is a legitimate design in which replicated within-tier changes carry evidence, but shared-history confounding is harder to evaluate across tiers.
column5: A nonconcurrent design that fully controls shared-history effects.
column8: OURS IS NONCONCURRENT. Names the specific weakness: a tier-specific event can imitate treatment in only that tier. Requires a per-window log of what else changed.

column2: Single-case designs require reporting measures, intervention delivery, fidelity, sequence, raw outcomes, adverse events and limitations.
column5: A reporting standard that omits adverse events or raw outcomes.
column8: SCRIBE 2016, reached via SRC-079 - which was READ IN FULL and names the required items explicitly (measures, intervention delivery, procedural fidelity, sequence, raw outcomes, ADVERSE EVENTS, limitations). The SCRIBE primary (SRC-080) was NOT fetched, so it is not relied on here; the chain of provenance is stated rather than implied.

column2: A component change can be a legitimate tier unit when the causal logic is defensible and the unit is stated explicitly.
column5: A design in which an arbitrary unit is accepted without stated causal logic.
column8: Justifies treating UPGRADES as cases, provided the unit is documented as such rather than left implicit.

column2: The the host harness session log records a per-session context-plugin set at user/message.data.source.plugin, present in 2,854 of 3,008 sessions (94.9%), as 19 distinct per-session sets with dated disappearances (user-approval last appears 2026-09-23, tool-goal 2026-09-10, cordis-host-runner 2026-09-16); the previously ratified position that plugin_set is historically unrecoverable is therefore too strong.
column5: A re-decode of the same corpus in which fewer than 2,854 of 3,008 logs carry user/message.data.source.plugin, or in which one of the 154 logs without it carries a plugin set under some other key.
column8: DIRECT COUNT plus one step of reasoning. Overturns the premise of CLM-COLLECT-04 for 94.9% of sessions; the 154 uncovered sessions stay genuinely unknown, so the capture_era discriminator is NOT thereby retired. The dated disappearances are consistent with plugins leaving the config, which is a change-impact event rather than a log-format limit.

column5: A re-decode in which model/selection appears in more than a small minority of sessions, or in which request/context and request/header do not each cover approximately 2,909 sessions, or their union not approximately 2,936.
column8: The session-3 read took model/selection as the model_set carrier; that event is a 0.23% outlier and would have produced a 99.77% false-negative rate. RECORD THE UNION COVERAGE, not either event alone. Also contradicts the session-3 STATUS.md line calling model_set unrecoverable.

column5: Any assistant/message record in a re-decode lacking message.source.model or its provider, or a session whose assistant records lack step/turn coordinates.
column8: DIRECT COUNT, exhaustive over the event type. CORRECTS an earlier measurement that reported only 1,484 of 187,770 steps resolved: that run read the WRONG EVENT, it is not missing data — the 1,484 figure must not be cited again. model_set is therefore recoverable PER STEP for the whole historical corpus, not only prospectively.

column2: reasoningEffort is carried only by request/header (2,464 occurrences across 1,861 sessions) and model/selection (11 occurrences across 6 sessions), covering 1,861 of 3,008 sessions (61.85%), and no per-step effort field exists anywhere in the log.
column5: A re-decode finding a reasoningEffort key on an assistant/message or on any other per-step record, or finding it in a session outside the 1,861 that request/header covers.
column8: The negative half is an exhaustive field-name scan of all 11,167,278 decoded records, not a sample. effort is therefore the WEAKEST of the four confounder axes: ~62% of the historical corpus, per session only, and per step only prospectively. The missing 38% must be modelled as effort-UNKNOWN, never as effort-default.

column2: max_depth is exactly recoverable for every session from the header record's delegationDepth field: present in 3,007 of 3,007 logs, values 0 (9.54%), 1 (55.34%), 2 (18.89%), 3 (16.23%), maximum observed 3; independently corroborated by delegationDepth > 0 holding if and only if a subagent/descriptor event is present.
column5: A session log whose header record lacks delegationDepth, or any session with delegationDepth = 0 that contains a subagent/descriptor event, or with delegationDepth > 0 that contains none.
column8: EXACT, not estimated. The if-and-only-if against subagent/descriptor is an independent path to the same partition, so the two cannot both be wrong through the same defect. UNRESOLVED AND RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: the corpus has 3,008 directories / 3,012 log files but only 3,007 header records, and this row does not explain the 5-session gap.

column2: subagent_spawns is NOT exactly recoverable from the session logs: only 1,055 of 2,717 parentSession edges (38.83%) resolve to a session log still on disk and the projection cache contains no spawn count at all, so the axis requires a union estimator combining the on-disk parent join with in-log 'started subagent <uuid>' matches, and its result must be declared an estimate rather than a count.
column5: A re-run of the parent join in which more than 1,055 of 2,717 parentSession edges resolve to a log on disk, or a projection-cache entry that exposes a per-session spawn count.
column8: The ONE axis of the four that is not exactly recoverable, and the shortfall is a RETENTION artefact (evicted or moved sessions), not a format limit — so more sessions on disk would raise coverage, not change the method. Any published spawn number is an estimate with a stated method and must never be compared against a count-derived number silently.

column2: The sandbox/approval/permission policy axes vary and change WITHIN sessions: sandbox/mode has 3 real values, approval/policy 2, permission/preset 4, at 100% coverage for top-level sessions, with 67 mid-session value changes corpus-wide; the canonical flip is permission/preset -> sandbox/mode -> approval/policy, triggered by a /permission danger-full-access command.
column5: A re-decode finding zero mid-session value changes for these three axes, or a top-level session in which any of the three changes value between its first and its last occurrence.
column8: DIRECT COUNTS plus the design consequence, which follows from them: THE SCHEMA MUST BE EVENT-SCOPED, NOT SESSION-SCOPED, for these three axes. A single per-session value silently picks one point of a 3-value flip and is not a summary of it. The /permission trigger is itself a change-impact event and belongs in the tier-specific event log required by CLM-MBD-05.

column2: The session header's agentPreset field undercounts the preset axis and must not be used as the confounder: 54 of 3,008 sessions lack it entirely, and the agent-preset/selected event records 4 distinct values including cordis and plugin-forge, which appear in no header record at all.
column5: A re-decode finding agentPreset present in all 3,008 headers, or finding no agent-preset/selected event at all, or finding cordis or plugin-forge in any header record.
column8: NAMES THE TRAP THIS ROW EXISTS TO CLOSE: a header-only read yields an axis with 2 of its 4 values invisible and 54 sessions missing, while looking complete. Use agent-preset/selected for the preset axis; treat the header field as a redundant hint, never as the axis.

column2: A naive text search for plugin package names across the corpus finds 532 distinct strings in 2,916 files that look like a plugin inventory but are free text (shell output and typed text); the only structural carrier of plugin identity is user/message.data.source.plugin.
column5: A re-decode showing that any of the 532 strings resolves to a structured inventory field rather than free text, or a structural plugin-identity carrier other than user/message.data.source.plugin.
column8: RECORDED SO A FUTURE READER CANNOT MISTAKE THE GREP FOR AN AXIS. A grep-based plugin inventory looks plausible and would conflate configuration with tool output, because the false positives are shell output and typed text, not configuration. Count the axis from CLM-CONF-01's structural field only.

column2: The the host harness session log injects skill-catalog contents into a session via events whose user/message.data.source.kind is 'skill-catalog'; the corpus contains 7 distinct catalog contents ranging from 2 to 28 skills, ~~with clean date boundaries between them~~ whose active windows overlap rather than partition the corpus: 6 of 21 catalog pairs share at least one UTC date, and on 4 dates (2026-09-23, 2026-09-24, 2026-09-25, 2026-09-26) two catalogs were in force within the SAME session; only 23 of 1,585 catalog-bearing sessions (1.45%) see more than one catalog, which is why 'clean' looked defensible and is not; and ~~in the re-ingested corpus the skill_catalog_set axis is populated for 51.0% of 3,017 sessions~~ THE COVERAGE FIGURE RESTATED ON THE CURRENT DENOMINATORS: the skill_catalog_set axis is populated for 51.81% of 3,067 sessions in the store rebuilt 2026-09-29 (1,589 of 3,067 non-empty) and 51.68% of the SAME 3,067 measured independently on the corpus side (1,585 of 3,067) — store and corpus now sit on ONE denominator. The move from 51.0% of 3,017 to 51.81% of 3,067 is DENOMINATOR-DRIVEN AND NOT A CHANGE IN BEHAVIOUR: the rate is flat to within the rounding and the entire difference is that 3,017 was a smaller earlier census of a corpus that is live and still growing. COVERAGE IS NOW 100% OF THE CENSUS: 3,067 store session records against 3,067 on-disk session directories, 3,071 log files, 4 of those directories holding a second generation. The corpus has since grown again to 3,074 directories / 3,078 log files, so against the live corpus the store is a snapshot at 3,067/3,074 = 99.77% — which is the denominator caveat restated, not a new discrepancy.
column5: A re-decode in which the distinct-catalog count is not 7 under any of the four equivalence definitions tried (exact entries including descriptions, exact ordered names, unordered name set, entry count alone), or in which no two catalog windows share a date, or in which fewer than 23 of the catalog-bearing sessions carry more than one catalog; or the axis populated for any share of sessions other than 51.81% of 3,067 in a store rebuilt from a corpus census of the same date (51.68% measured directly on the corpus side — store and corpus on one denominator, so neither is a free parameter and the two are directly comparable). A share that moves ONLY because the corpus grew between the census and the re-ingest is NOT a falsification: the denominator is the moving part here, so compare rates and never compare a raw count against an older denominator. SRC-081's live-corpus caveat governs the direction of that allowance.
column8: ADDS THE ROW THAT N10 REQUIRED BEFORE THE NUMBER COULD BE USED: a previous worker refused to write '7 catalog contents' because no row backed it, and flagged the gap instead of breaking the rule. ~~'Clean boundaries' is a claim about NON-INTERLEAVING first/last occurrences, which the falsifier tests directly.~~ CORRECTED 2026-09-29, VISIBLY AND NOT DELETED: an independent decode of 3,067 session logs / 2.36 GB / 6,398,508 zstd frames fired this row's own 'two catalog contents in force on the same date' branch, so the clause is struck and the falsifier was rewritten to the falsified shape. CONVENTION USED: this ledger has no strikethrough precedent and only the status value 'active' in use, so the workspace's prose correction convention (AGENTS.md N6, PRODUCT.md N6, ARCHITECTURE.md §7 — strike the old wording, then state the correction) was carried into the claim text rather than inventing a new status. The row stays 'active' because it is corrected, not superseded. WHAT SURVIVED UNCHANGED: the count of 7 holds under all four equivalence definitions tried, and the sizes are exactly 2, 3, 8, 15, 23, 24, 28, so the 2-28 range is exact rather than merely observed. THE NEAR MISS: only 23 of 1,585 catalog-bearing sessions see more than one catalog, so the catalogs nearly partition sessions, which is exactly why 'clean' looked defensible; 7 of 21 pairs overlap by file-mtime date rather than 6 of 21 by UTC date. PRESENCE RATE, NOT IDENTITY — STILL TRUE, STILL THE IMPORTANT ONE, AND THE FIX DOES NOT CHANGE IT: the figure is the share of sessions in which a catalog was injected AT ALL. Now that the axis carries catalog identity (CLM-CONF-11, fixed and verified in the store) it is tempting to read a coverage percentage off it, and that would be wrong: the percentage still counts only sessions where a catalog was injected, the 1,478 empty arrays sit in the denominator as 'no catalog', and nothing in 51.81% says WHICH catalog was in force. It remains a presence rate and must not be cited as coverage of catalog identity. What the fix did change is only that the store can now answer the separate identity question, which it could not when this note was written. DENOMINATOR CAVEAT (still correct, keep, restated against the rebuild): the denominator is the RE-INGEST session total — 3,067 as of the 2026-09-29 rebuild — and is not SRC-081's original 3,008-directory census, so the coverage figure is NOT comparable to CLM-CONF-01's 94.9%; and because the corpus is live the denominator keeps moving, which is exactly why this row's falsifier is now written against rates on a stated census date rather than against a fixed count. ~~Both sides of the verification now agree on numerator: store 1,539 / 3,017 = 51.01%, corpus 1,585 / 3,067 = 51.68%, and the entire gap is the denominator, because the corpus is live and grew during the measurement.~~ THE TWO SIDES NOW AGREE ON BOTH NUMERATOR AND DENOMINATOR: store 1,589 / 3,067 = 51.81% against corpus 1,585 / 3,067 = 51.68%, leaving a 0.13-point residual that is not a disagreement about behaviour. COUNTING TRAP FOR THE NEXT REPRODUCER: the store holds 3,079 session-rung RECORDS but only 3,067 distinct session ids — 12 ids are put twice — so 3,067 is the figure after de-duplicating last-put-wins and 3,079 is a row count, not a session count. SOURCING (corrects this row's own tail): the counts were NOT 'sourced as given' — the verification re-derived them. AS OF THE 2026-09-29 REBUILD both figures come from that ingest: store 1,589 / 3,067 and corpus 1,585 / 3,067, with the store side re-measured independently from app/data/observation/2026-09-29.jsonl for this edit and the corpus side from a 400-directory decode that returned 52.00%, consistent with 51.68% within sampling noise.

column2: The store's confounders.confounders.skill_catalog_set axis ~~is a PRESENCE FLAG WEARING A SET'S NAME, not a skill set: it is literally ["catalog"] in 1,539 of 1,539 occurrences, set size always 1~~ NOW CARRIES THE CATALOG ENTRY LIST ITSELF, VERIFIED IN THE STORE BY A CLEAN REBUILD: the axis holds exactly 7 distinct NON-EMPTY values, of set size 2, 3, 8, 15, 23, 24 and 28 (occurrences 23→669, 15→258, 28→250, 24→216, 8→188, 2→6, 3→2), and the other 1,478 of 3,067 session records carry an EMPTY array, which is an honest absence and not a placeholder. ZERO occurrences hold the 9-character string "catalog" WITH double quotes, zero hold the bare 7-character string catalog, and no array contains the substring at all. THE SPELLING AMBIGUITY, MADE EXPLICIT BECAUSE IT IS THE WHOLE CONFUSION: the pre-fix value rendered as the array dump ["catalog"], which reads as a one-element array containing the word catalog; it was neither the bare word nor a set of skills — it was the single 9-character string "catalog", quotes included, the output of JSON.stringify('catalog'). ~~because it is populated from user/message.data.source.form, a constant, rather than from the catalog itself~~ THE ERROR WAS, AND THE CORRECTION IS: the bug class is a WRONG FIELD PATH PLUS A HARDCODED DEFAULT, not a mis-selected field. The pre-fix adapter read data['entries'] (app/src/adapters/host harness.ts:760-763) — one level ABOVE the real location user/message.data.source.entries — so the value was ALWAYS undefined and data.source.form was NEVER READ AT ALL; control therefore reached the hardcoded fallback literal JSON.stringify(entries ?? 'catalog'). The stored element is the 9-character string "catalog" WITH double quotes (the output of JSON.stringify('catalog')), NOT the bare 7-character string catalog; a store dump renders it as ["catalog"], which is where the ambiguity came from, and the live test failure confirms the distinction (expected [ '"catalog"' ] to deeply equal [...]). The catalog is user/message.data.source.entries, an array whose every entry carries exactly the two keys name and description, data.source.form is always the literal 'catalog', data.source.update is true on repeat injections and absent on the first, and there is NO STABLE CATALOG IDENTIFIER anywhere, so the entry list is the only identity and any distinct-catalog count is a choice of equivalence relation rather than a measurement of a declared identity.
column5: A re-ingest in which any skill_catalog_set occurrence holds the 9-character string "catalog" or the bare 7-character string catalog, or in which any NON-EMPTY occurrence's set size is not one of 2, 3, 8, 15, 23, 24, 28, or in which any non-empty value is not the sorted, de-duplicated set of the name fields of that session's own data.source.entries; or a re-decode in which data.source.entries is absent, is not an array, or carries any entry key beyond name and description; or in which data.source.form is ever anything but the literal 'catalog', or in which data.source.update is present on a first injection or absent on a repeat; or in which the corpus exposes a stable catalog identifier (a version, id or hash carried by the injection) that makes the distinct-catalog count independent of the equivalence relation chosen. THE COUNT OF 7 IS TO BE READ AGAINST A STATED CENSUS DATE, NEVER AGAINST THE LIVE CORPUS: an eighth catalog appearing in later sessions is corpus growth, not a falsification, and SRC-081's live-corpus caveat governs. An empty array is an absence, not a set size to be falsified.
column8: ~~DEFECT MEASURED, CORRECTED SEMANTICS NOT YET BACK IN THE STORE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE STRENGTH ARGUMENT. The false axis was counted over the re-ingested store (1,539 / 1,539 occurrences carrying ["catalog"], set size 1 in every single one), so nothing here is reasoned and nothing is disputed. STRENGTH CHOSEN FROM THE VALUES ALREADY IN USE (established / supported / contested / inference): 'inference' is wrong because this is counted, not argued; 'contested' is wrong because no one is disputing it; 'established' would assert the store already carries the corrected axis, and it does not — the corrected semantics are read off the on-disk injection events and are specified but NOT yet re-ingested; 'supported' is the only value that fits a measured defect plus a specified-but-unre-ingested fix.~~ DEFECT FIXED AND VERIFIED END-TO-END 2026-09-29, AND THE STRENGTH IS RAISED supported → established: the call, then the argument, not the reverse. THE STORE WAS DELETED AND REGENERATED FROM THE CORPUS (rm -rf app/data && pnpm ingest — 71.0 s, exit 0) and THIS ROW'S OWN FALSIFIER FIRED BY DESIGN — the pre-fix branch ("any occurrence holds a value other than ["catalog"], or any occurrence's set size is not 1") is true of the rebuilt store at 7 distinct values and set sizes 2/3/8/15/23/24/28, so the defect state is gone. The reason recorded against 'established' was that the store did not yet carry the corrected axis; that condition no longer holds and nothing replaces it. What remains is an exhaustive, reproducible, directly quotable count over SRC-081, a primary and verified source, on the same evidentiary footing as the three sibling rows already at 'established' (CLM-CONF-03, -04, -05), every one of which is a single-census measurement of this same corpus and every one of which is bounded by the same live-corpus caveat. Holding this row at 'supported' would have left a justification in this cell that is no longer true and made it inconsistent with its three siblings for no defensible reason. WHAT 'established' DOES AND DOES NOT COVER, so a later reader can downgrade it with reasons: it carries the MEASURED half — the defect is closed, the axis now holds the entry list, the 7 values and their set sizes are as stated. It does NOT harden the universal negative "there is NO STABLE CATALOG IDENTIFIER anywhere", which holds only as of this census and decays as the corpus grows, nor "any distinct-catalog count is a choice of equivalence relation rather than a measurement of a declared identity", which is THIS PROJECT'S REASONING over the measured fact and is the honest reason to prefer 'supported'. RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY FOR THIS EDIT RATHER THAN TAKEN ON REPORT: decoding app/data/observation/2026-09-29.jsonl (433,269 records) and de-duplicating session-rung records last-put-wins gives 3,067 sessions, 1,589 non-empty (51.81%) and exactly the 7 sizes and occurrence counts above, with zero elements equal to "catalog" or to catalog; a separate 400-directory decode of the on-disk corpus returned 52.00% catalog-bearing, entry key sets {description,name} only, and data.source.form === 'catalog' on all 328 injections seen. THE ROW STAYS 'active', corrected and not superseded; no new status value was invented. WHY IT WAS A CONFOUNDER DEFECT AND NOT COSMETIC — the pre-fix state, kept because it is why the row exists: the axis had 1 distinct value where the corpus has 7, so every catalog-bearing session was recorded as identical on the skill axis and any per-catalog comparison was silently unidentifiable; a query that grouped or filtered on this axis could not tell two catalogs apart and reported them as one group. Both failures are repaired and verified; the defect is now history. THIS IS WHY CLM-CONF-10's COVERAGE FIGURE SURVIVES: it is a PRESENCE rate, blind to which catalog was in force, so the broken axis never falsified it — and populating the axis correctly does not turn it into an identity rate, because a populated axis still says only THAT a catalog was injected. What the fix changes is that the store can now answer the identity question at all, which it could not when this was written. NO STABLE ID IS THE ROOT CAUSE, NOT THE DISPLAY, AND THE FIX DID NOT CHANGE IT: because the entry list is the only identity, the seven-count in CLM-CONF-10 is robust only in the empirical sense that all four equivalence relations tried agree on 7; that robustness is a property of this corpus, not a guarantee for future ones, and a future catalog that is a strict superset of another under one relation and equal under another would split the count. FIX LOCATION, CORRECTED VISIBLY 2026-09-29 AND NOT DELETED: ~~app/src/adapters/host harness.ts — the skill-catalog branch that reads data.source.form where it should read data.source.entries~~ THE ERROR WAS. THE MECHANISM, FROM app/src/adapters/host harness.ts:760-763 (PRE-FIX): `const entries = (data['entries'] ?? source.name) as unknown` read one level above the real location data.source.entries, so the read always yielded undefined; data.source.form was NEVER read; and because source.name is likewise absent in the real corpus the ?? fallback never fired either. Control therefore always reached `JSON.stringify(entries ?? 'catalog')` — a HARDCODED literal, not a field read. BUG CLASS: a wrong field path plus a hardcoded default. STORED VALUE, PRECISELY: the element is the 9-character string "catalog" WITH double quotes, the output of JSON.stringify('catalog'), NOT the bare 7-character string `catalog`; the array dump renders as ["catalog"], which is where the ambiguity came from. ~~The corrected axis should carry the entry list (or a stable hash of it) from data.source.entries, and form/update should be kept as metadata alongside it rather than as the axis value.~~ AS BUILT, AND IT IS NOT EXACTLY WHAT WAS ASKED FOR: the shipped axis carries the entry NAMES — the sorted, de-duplicated set of each entry's name field (app/src/adapters/host harness.ts:779-784 and :1102) — not the {name, description} objects and not a hash of them; and form/update are NOT retained beside it as metadata, they are simply not read at all. Descriptions are therefore dropped. That is consistent with CLM-CONF-10's four equivalence definitions only because all four were name-based; an entry set differing in description alone would count as ONE catalog under the shipped axis. Recorded as a difference, not as a defect. ~~ACTION STILL OUTSTANDING: the store must be re-ingested before this axis is used for any published comparison; until then every skill_catalog_set value in the store is a constant and must not be treated as a confounder value.~~ DISCHARGED 2026-09-29: the re-ingest is done, so this axis may now be used for published comparisons, subject to the two standing caveats above — the census date, and the absence of a stable identifier.

column2: The cockpit ingest re-appended one observation id 34 times in 4.33 s (id b47f493f-32e5-4aa4-8ed4-74e9d7d799f8:step:1:13, rung step, put sequence numbers 428438-428473 on the pre-fix store), and the mechanism is that an in-flight record can BE the cursor: the per-event gate is inclusive of the cursor (if (e.time < sinceMs) continue) and the next cursor is the maximum ts among the observations yielded (app/src/plugins/adapters.ts:132-135, :139), while ts is a DERIVED field that an observation still in flight stamps as its own start time (ts: iso(end?.time ?? e.time), app/src/adapters/host harness.ts:981 and :1018) - the very value the gate tests - so the row is simultaneously the batch maximum and the cursor, the cursor can never advance past it, and the slice loop only exits on a zero-yield poll, so a pinned tail never terminates. The 34 appends were NOT byte-identical: they differed only in provenance[0].ingested_at, which is re-stamped on every append, which is why a content-hash guard cannot fix this. FIXED by a boundary-id gate that admits records whose event time equals the cursor once, keyed on the observation id (BoundaryGate, app/src/adapters/host harness.ts:209-259; opened at :564, consulted at :688). VERIFIED by a clean rebuild (rm -rf app/data && pnpm ingest, exit 0): 433,221 put lines / 433,221 distinct ids / excess 0 / zero duplicate ids, and by a forced second poll: 433,269 put / 433,256 distinct / excess 13, of which ALL 13 are DIFFERING records (a legitimate supersede) and ZERO are identical re-appends. THE CORRECT POST-FIX CONDITION IS ZERO IDENTICAL RE-APPENDS, NOT ZERO DUPLICATES - the excess of 13 is real and is not a defect, so 'zero duplicates' would be the wrong claim and is not what was measured.

column8: STRENGTH established, and the argument is the CLM-CONF-11 one applied consistently, not a new bar. CLM-CONF-11 was held at supported precisely because the store did not yet carry the corrected state, and was raised when a clean rebuild put it there. That condition no longer holds here: the store on disk is post-fix and the post-fix condition was independently re-measured for this edit (433,269 put / 433,256 distinct / excess 13 / 0 identical). The mechanism half is quotable from source with line numbers, and the fix is in the code and in a named class, so both halves sit on primary, verified evidence - the same footing as the sibling CLM-CONF rows. WHAT 'established' COVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT, so this can be downgraded with reasons: it covers the mechanism (source, line numbers), the existence of the defect as an OBSERVED event (34 appends, 4.33 s, seq 428438-428473, plus a 34-poll probe that reproduced it exactly), and the post-fix condition. It does NOT cover the 34-append measurement as a currently re-checkable fact - the pre-fix store was deleted by rm -rf app/data and the CLM-CONF- series is uncommitted, so neither the artefact nor the pre-fix code survives in git. Anyone re-verifying must reproduce the defect against pre-fix code, not re-read the store. THE STATISTICAL TRAP, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE OBVIOUS WAY TO GET THIS ROW WRONG: excess>0 in an append-only log is not evidence of a bug, because a second poll legitimately re-emits a changed record and last-put-wins. The pre-fix duplicate was NOT a duplicate id in the set sense either - it was one id written 34 times with a re-stamped provenance block, so a naive distinct-id count alone would have found it and a naive byte-comparison alone would have declared it clean. Both checks are required: distinct-id count AND body comparison. WHY THE FIX IS KEYED ON id AND NOT ON A CONTENT HASH, which is the non-obvious constraint: ingested_at is re-stamped on every append, so a hash guard never matches and fixes nothing. WHY NOT THE ONE-WORD EXCLUSIVE GATE (e.time <= sinceMs): several events share a millisecond, so an exclusive gate would drop every sibling emitted in the cursor's own millisecond. Both alternatives were considered and rejected in source. BOUNDED, NOT ELIMINATED, AND SAID SO RATHER THAN OVERSTATED: the gate is process-local and holds one millisecond's ids, so a restart can re-emit at most that one millisecond once. That is a bounded, self-correcting duplicate in an append-only log, not a growing one. GENERALISATION THIS ROW ESTABLISHES FOR THE READER, and it is the lesson the session drew: ts is a DERIVED field, so any gate that tests ts can be defeated by a record that derives ts from the value being tested. Gate on a stable identity or admit nothing - a cursor and a content value are not the same kind of thing. SCOPE: this is a claim about the cockpit adapter and store, not about the the host harness corpus; it is measured against SRC-082 and is deliberately NOT attributed to SRC-081, which covers the corpus census. Status active; no new status value invented. RELATES TO, DOES NOT TOUCH: CLM-CONF-04 and CLM-CONF-11 are the two sibling defects of the same four-defect set that already had rows.

column2: The cockpit adapter's file-level skip in DshAdapter.pullBatches was an UNCONDITIONAL if (last < sinceMs) continue that ran BEFORE effectiveSince was computed and did not test whether the file was already known, so the first time a session log was seen, if the cursor had already advanced past that session's last event, the whole file was read and then discarded silently - no record, no warning - and the index entry written just before the skip made every later poll treat the same file as known-and-settled. FIXED by gating the skip on the index entry (if (known && last < sinceMs) continue, app/src/adapters/host harness.ts:609), which also revives the previously unreachable branch effectiveSince = known ? sinceMs : 0 (:621), which had been dead for every file older than the cursor. THE DEFECT IS LATENT AND WAS NEVER OBSERVED TO HAVE COST DATA: at the time of measurement 3,059 session directories existed on disk against 3,017 store records, a shortfall of 42, and ALL 42 were provably NEWER than the run's final cursor (store max session ts 15:38:16.410Z against the oldest missing session's last event 15:48:16.018Z, and every one of the 42 log mtimes fell after the store's last write at 15:41:08.700Z), so the shortfall was ordinary ingest lag and not loss. It cannot fire on a first full pass, where sinceMs === 0; it needs a poll that discovers an already-old file while the cursor is high - a bounded or resumable catch-up pass, or a deleted index cache.
column5: A run of app/tests/host harness-adapter.spec.ts in which the silent-drop case at :761-809 passes with the fix REVERTED (i.e. reverting :609 to an unconditional 'if (last < sinceMs) continue' does NOT make it fail on 'session-ancient', or it fails for any reason other than the file's absence - the failure must be the silent absence, not an error); or a reading of app/src/adapters/host harness.ts in which the skip is again unconditional, or in which effectiveSince is not 'known ? sinceMs : 0'; or an ingest run over real data in which a session directory present on disk is neither present in the store NOR newer than the run's final cursor - that would be a first provable instance of cost and would upgrade this row's evidence, not falsify the mechanism; or a reading of :621 in which a never-seen file can be cursor-filtered. Conversely the claim is NOT falsified by the absence of lost data: the 42-session shortfall was measured as ordinary lag, and the row asserts LATENCY, not a loss, so 'no data was actually lost' leaves this row standing. If a future bounded catch-up pass runs and loses nothing, the mechanism is still in the code and the row is still true.
column8: STRENGTH supported, DELIBERATELY ONE STEP BELOW ITS SIBLING CLM-CONF-12, and the difference is the finding rather than a matter of taste. CLM-CONF-12's defect was OBSERVED FIRING on real data and its fix was verified against a rebuilt store. This one was NEVER OBSERVED FIRING on real data at all: the 42 missing sessions were provably all newer than the final cursor, so the shortfall was lag, not loss. 'established' would assert more than the evidence carries - that the defect was real in operation, which is precisely the thing that was not measured, and this workspace's rule is that a claim without its evidence must not be asserted. 'inference' is wrong because the mechanism is not argued, it is read off the source with line numbers and proven by a fail-then-pass test. 'contested' is wrong because nobody disputes it. 'supported' fits: one source with measured results (SRC-082), where the result is a code reading plus a synthetic regression test and the loss count is zero. THE ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE POINT: ~~two of the four defects in this verification pass had rows and two did not~~ - true when this note was written, which is precisely why this row and CLM-CONF-12 exist, and false as a statement of current state; adding the weaker one at the same strength as the stronger one would smooth away the distinction the documentation was making when it flagged these as unledgered. CORRECTED 2026-09-29, VISIBLY AND NOT DELETED: only the first clause is struck, because all four defects of that verification pass now have rows - CLM-CONF-04 and CLM-CONF-11 already had them, CLM-CONF-12 and CLM-CONF-13 are the other two - so nothing in the set is unledgered and a reader must not infer that this row or CLM-CONF-12 is missing. THE DOCUMENTATION FLAG WAS WITHDRAWN IN THE SAME STEP, WHICH IS WHY THAT CLAUSE IS KEPT AND NOT STRUCK: AGENTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md no longer say these defects lack a row and now cite CLM-CONF-12 and CLM-CONF-13 on SRC-082, so 'the documentation was making ... when it flagged these as unledgered' is history about the state that produced this row, not a claim about the documentation today. WHAT SURVIVES AND STILL CARRIES THE POINT: the asymmetry is now a difference in EVIDENCE between two ledgered rows - this one at supported because the defect was never observed firing on real data, CLM-CONF-12 at established because it was - and not a gap between a rowed and an unrowed defect. A later reader can raise this to established the moment a real loss is observed, and the notes say exactly what that evidence is. FAIL-THEN-PASS, which is the only honest way to verify a bug that never fires: with the fix reverted the new test fails with 'expected [...] to include session-ancient' - the silent absence, no error thrown, which is the whole character of the defect. A test that passed before the fix would prove nothing, and a test that failed with an error would be testing a different bug. WHY IT WAS WORTH A ROW AT ALL, given zero measured cost: it is latent, not harmless. A single token on :609 gates an entire session log out of the store with no diagnostic, and the failure mode it enables - a resumable catch-up pass that silently ingests none of its backlog - is on the project's own build order, not hypothetical. The index entry written just before the skip is what makes it permanent: one silent discard converts a never-seen file into a known-and-settled one, so no later poll will ever revisit it. THE SAME ROOT SHAPE AS CLM-CONF-12, AND WORTH NAMING: both defects are the same error class - a control-flow decision made before the state that would qualify it was computed, so the decision was unconditional where it had to be conditional. That is the transferable lesson, and it is the reason a unit-test-green adapter was not evidence of correctness.
